newsitem.title: USA: NYC bonding authority bill to pass-state lawmakers.
newsitem.headline: NYC bonding authority bill to pass-state lawmakers.

text.p: The leaders of the New York State Senate and Assembly said Wednesday that legislation creating a new bond authority for New York City will pass.

Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, a Democrat, said he expected passage of the legislation, which would allow the city to create a new, temporary bonding authority to sell up to $7.5 billion of debt and bypass a debt-cap ceiling.
Senate Leader Joseph Bruno, a Republican, also said the bill will pass.
Both chambers of the legislature are expected to vote on the measure Wednesday.

The legislation also calls for a constitutional amendment that would establish a new debt cap reflecting a broader city revenue base than just that gained from real property taxes. The declining value of New York City's real estate market has led to declining bonding potential.

The city usually sells between $2 billion and $4 billion of general obligation debt annually. But a debt cap triggered by outstanding debt could bring a halt to bond sales later this year. The new, temporary authority would allow the city to continue bond sales.
